hottest.summary: Overview On November 19, 2026, Broadcom published VMware Security Advisory VMSA-2026-0009 , addressing five vulnerabilities in VMware products. The most severe of these, CVE-2026-123890 , is an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel ( CWE-288 ) in the VMware Directory Service component of vCenter. Broadcom assigned the vulnerability a critical CVSSv3 score of 9.8 . A malicious actor with network access to an affected vCenter deployment may exploit CVE-2026-123890 without credentials to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system as the Administrator user. Mandiant privately reported the issue to Broadcom. Also, Mandiant/Google Threat Intelligence confirmed in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-123890 by Chinese state-linked threat actor ARMORY CASTLE as early as September 2026. CVE-2026-123890 is distinct from the vCenter authentication bypass vulnerability CVE-2026-59309 that Broadcom addressed earlier in 2026. The vendor FAQ states that all vCenter systems below the versions fixed by VMSA-2026-0009 require the new update, including systems that already received the earlier fix. Broadcom characterizes the vCenter update as an emergency change requiring prompt action. Mitigation guidance Vendor-provided updates are available for CVE-2026-123890. Broadcom lists no workaround, and the patches cannot be applied using vCenter Quick Patch. Organizations should prioritize upgrading vCenter on an emergency basis, outside of normal patch cycles, using the standard update mechanism for their deployment. VMware Product Affected Version Fixed Version / Patch VMware Cloud Foundation / vSphere Foundation 9.1.x.x 9.1.1.0200 VMware Cloud Foundation / vSphere Foundation 9.0.x.x 9.0.2.0200 VMware vCenter Server 8.0 8.0 U3m VMware vCenter Server 7.0 Contact Broadcom Support (extended-support customers) VMware Cloud Foundation 5.x 5.2.5 VMware Telco Cloud Platform 3.0, 4.x, 5.0.x, 5.1.x, 5.2 8.0 U3m — KB463116 VMware Telco Cloud Infrastructure 3.0 8.0 U3m — KB463116 The fixes are cumulative. The vCenter 8.0 U3m and 9.0.2.0200 updates introduce a “Back-in-Time” restriction that blocks upgrades to VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.1 ; Broadcom advises customers in an active upgrade to review the vendor FAQ and interoperability matrix. Updating vCenter temporarily makes its management interfaces unavailable, but Broadcom states that running virtual machine and container workloads continue to operate. For the latest affected-version and mitigation guidance, please refer to Broadcom's security advisory and supplemental FAQ . Rapid7 customers Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose Exposure Command, InsightVM, and Nexpose customers can assess exposure to CVE-2026-123890 on VMware vCenter Server with an unauthenticated vulnerability check expected to be available in the Nov 20, 2026 content release. Updates November 19, 2026 : Initial publication.

persistent_hot.summary: Overview On November 17, 2026, Oracle released patches for CVE-2026-114938 , a heap-based buffer overflow ( CWE-122 ) in the hardware-accelerated Base64 decoder used by OpenJDK and its downstream distributions, such as Oracle Java SE, and Oracle GraalVM. The vulnerability, dubbed “ Java4Shell ” by finders Calif, can allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to crash a Java application or execute code with the privileges of its Java process. Oracle rates the vulnerability High, with a CVSS v3.1 score of 8.1 and high attack complexity, in its November security advisory . Affected OpenJDK runtimes enable the vulnerable Base64 optimization by default when the Java virtual machine (JVM) can use the required x86-64 CPU features, including AVX-512 VBMI. A Java application exposes the flaw when it passes untrusted data to that optimized decoder. For example, a web service may decode HTTP Basic credentials before it checks the username and password. Red Hat reports no known exposure on ARM64 or on x86-64 processors without AVX-512 VBMI in its OpenJDK bulletin . Calif’s disclosure states that they demonstrated unauthenticated remote code execution against several popular Java based applications, and they have published a local proof of concept (PoC) for CVE-2026-114938, which can test if a local JDK is vulnerable. Given the ubiquitous nature of Java and its deployment across enterprise environments, Rapid7 recommends identifying and remediating affected systems, with a focus on Internet exposed systems, on an emergency basis and outside of normal patching cycles. Rapid7 is actively monitoring the situation and will update this blog as new information arrives. For the latest vendor release information, refer to Oracle's November security update notice and OpenJDK's vulnerability advisories . Technical overview CVE-2026-114938 affects a hardware-specific optimization in HotSpot, the Java virtual machine used by many OpenJDK distributions. When frequently used Base64 decoding code is compiled, HotSpot can substitute a native routine that processes multiple bytes at once. The vulnerable path requires an x86-64 runtime, CPU features including AVX-512 VBMI , and effective JVM settings that permit the optimizing compiler and Base64 intrinsic. Consequently, an affected Java version alone does not establish that a particular application is exploitable. The defect occurs when that routine processes a malformed final Base64 group. Its calculation of the remaining output length can become negative, enabling a wider memory write than the destination can accommodate. Confirmed malformed-tail cases produce a 64-byte store extending 62 or 63 bytes beyond the calculated decoded-output length. Java subsequently rejects the malformed input, but catching that exception does not undo the corruption. Damage to another object can remain unnoticed until later activity, including garbage collection, crashes the JVM. Turning this constrained overwrite into code execution requires additional work. A reliable exploit typically needs to influence which objects occupy the affected memory, convert the initial corruption into useful access to other objects, and identify application or runtime behavior that permits further execution. The practical outcome therefore depends on the application, JVM build, memory layout, and security boundaries. This distinction explains why a working corruption trigger does not establish a portable exploit for every Java service. Remote exposure arises when an application passes attacker-controlled data to the affected decoder. Authentication headers and tokens are relevant examples, but reachability must be established for the actual implementation. The published OpenJDK fix hands final groups shorter than four bytes to the ordinary Java decoder. Organizations should apply their runtime vendor's fixed build and restart affected JVMs; disabling Base64 intrinsics with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics is a temporary mitigation where supported. Mitigation guidance Rapid7 recommends applying the November security update as soon as possible, starting with internet-facing services that decode credentials or tokens before authentication. Identify the runtime vendor and full build each service uses, including Java runtimes bundled with applications, appliances, and container images. OpenJDK lists release versions 17, 21, 25, and 27 as affected by CVE-2026-114938 in its November 17 advisory . Red Hat identifies OpenJDK 17.0.6 as the earliest affected version 17. Oracle separately identifies its Java 8 Enterprise Performance Pack as affected in the Java risk matrix . The table below pairs affected Oracle builds with the November updates listed in the JDK security baselines , Enterprise Performance Pack release notes , and GraalVM release calendar . Product Name Vulnerable Java Version Patched Version (Official Release Notes) Oracle Java SE 8 Performance Edition 8u511b33-perf 8u513-perf Oracle Java SE 17 17.0.21.0.3 17.0.21.1 Oracle Java SE 21 21.0.13.0.3 21.0.13.1 Oracle Java SE 25 25.0.5.0.3 25.0.5.1 Oracle Java SE 27 27.0.1.0.3 27.0.1.1 Oracle GraalVM for JDK 17 17.0.21.0.3 17.0.21.1 Oracle GraalVM for JDK 21 21.0.13.0.3 21.0.13.1 Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition 21.3.20.0.3 21.3.20.1 For other OpenJDK based distributions, use the patched package from your Java vendor. If an application or appliance bundles Java, use the product vendor’s update. Rebuild affected container images, redeploy the workloads, and restart affected services. Verify that each running Java process uses the patched build, as CIRCL recommends . If you cannot patch an affected OpenJDK service immediately, restart its JVM with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics . This disables hardware acceleration for Base64 decoding while leaving other CPU optimizations in place. Rapid7 customers To learn how to use Rapid7 capabilities to find systems affected by this vulnerability and for answers to common questions, read the Oracle OpenJDK Java (CVE-2026-114938) documentation . Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose customers can assess exposure to CVE-2026-114938 with authenticated vulnerability checks available to the scan engine and Rapid7 Agent. As of the November 18, content release ( 1.1.4119 ), the checks match the OpenJDK and Oracle advisories: A check for Java from any vendor flags the versions below. Each range runs up to, but not including, the fixed version.
